concepts.def: Density is how much mass a material packs into each unit of volume. Because it is a ratio, it belongs to the material rather than to the lump of material: a small piece and a large piece of the same metal at the same temperature have the same density.
The specification defines density by density = mass / volume. Mass goes on the top and volume on the bottom, so for a fixed mass a larger volume always means a smaller density.

In the symbol form of the equation, written as rho = m/V, rho stands for density, m stands for mass and V stands for volume. The symbols are not initials of the words, which is why they have to be learned.
The specification gives density, rho, in kilograms per metre cubed, kg/m^3. The unit follows straight from the equation: a mass in kilograms divided by a volume in metres cubed.
Mass, m, is measured in kilograms, kg. A balance usually reads in grams, so a reading in grams must be divided by 1000 before it is used to obtain a density in kg/m^3.
Volume, V, is measured in metres cubed, m^3. For a regular solid the volume is found by multiplying length by width by height. A volume in cm^3 must be divided by 1 000 000 to convert it to m^3.
One gram per centimetre cubed is one thousand kilograms per metre cubed, so a density in g/cm^3 is multiplied by 1000 to give kg/m^3. Water is 1.0 g/cm^3, which is 1000 kg/m^3.

The particle model pictures a substance as a very large number of tiny particles in constant motion. Their spacing and arrangement explain both the three states of matter and the differences in density between those states.
In a solid the particles are packed closely together in a fixed, regular arrangement and vibrate about fixed positions. A solid therefore keeps its own shape and has a fixed volume.

In a liquid the particles are still close together and touching, but the arrangement is random and the particles can move past one another. A liquid keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container.
In a gas the particles are far apart, arranged randomly and moving quickly in all directions. A gas has no fixed shape or volume and fills whatever container it is put in.

A simple diagram uses identical circles for the particles. A solid is drawn as circles touching in a regular pattern, a liquid as circles touching in a random pattern, and a gas as widely separated circles. The circles are the same size in all three diagrams.

For the same substance the particles have the same mass in every state, so density depends only on how closely they are packed. Solids and liquids have similar, high densities; a gas has a much lower density because the same particles are spread through a far larger volume.

For a regularly shaped object the mass is found on a balance and the volume is calculated from measured dimensions, for example length x width x height for a cuboid. Density is then the mass divided by that volume.

For an irregularly shaped object the volume is found by lowering it into a measuring cylinder of water, or into a displacement can, and recording the volume of water pushed out of the way. The volume of the object is the rise in level, that is the final reading minus the starting reading.

The mass of the empty measuring cylinder is recorded, a measured volume of liquid is poured in, and the cylinder is weighed again. The mass of the liquid is the difference between the two readings, and that mass is divided by the measured volume.

A ruler is suitable for lengths of a few centimetres, Vernier callipers resolve to about 0.1 mm and suit small objects, and a micrometer resolves to about 0.01 mm and suits thin wires and sheets. The instrument is chosen so that its resolution is small compared with the length being measured.
Melting, freezing, boiling, evaporating, condensing and subliming are changes of state. The particles gain or lose energy and rearrange, but no particles are created or destroyed.

concepts.term: Conservation of mass in a change of state
concepts.def: When a substance changes state the number of particles and the mass of each particle are unchanged, so the total mass is unchanged. A balance reading only falls because gas has escaped from the container, not because mass has vanished.

A change of state is a physical change: no new substance is made, and reversing the change returns the material to its original properties. In a chemical change new substances are formed and the original properties are not recovered by simply reversing the conditions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the definition of the density of a material?
options: The volume the sample fills divided by its own mass.
The mass of the sample multiplied by the volume.
The mass of the sample divided by its volume.
The total mass the sample happens to have.
mcqs.explain: This is the definition the specification gives: density = mass / volume.

mcqs.q: In the equation ρ = m/V, what do the symbols m and V stand for?
options: m stands for mass and V stands for volume.
m stands for metres and V stands for volume.
m stands for mass and V is the speed it moves.
m stands for the weight and V for the volume.
mcqs.explain: These are the quantities the specification lists for this equation: mass, m, in kilograms and volume, V, in metres cubed.

mcqs.q: Which unit does the specification use for density?
options: kilograms times metres cubed, kg m³
kilograms per metre squared, kg/m²
kilograms per metre cubed, written kg/m³
grams per centimetre cubed, g/cm³
mcqs.explain: The specification gives density, ρ, in kilograms per metre cubed, kg/m^3, which follows from dividing a mass in kg by a volume in m^3.

mcqs.q: A cube of steel has sides of 0.10 m and a mass of 7.8 kg. What is its density?
options: 7800 kg/m³
780 kg/m³
78 kg/m³

mcqs.q: A liquid has a density of 800 kg/m³. What volume is occupied by 2.0 kg of the liquid?
options: 400 m³
mcqs.explain: Rearranging ρ = m/V gives V = m/ρ = 2.0 / 800 = 0.0025 m^3.

mcqs.q: Aluminium has a density of 2.7 g/cm³. What is this density in kg/m³?
options: 2.7 kg/m³
2700 kg/m³
27 kg/m³
mcqs.explain: One g/cm^3 is 1000 kg/m^3, so 2.7 g/cm^3 x 1000 = 2700 kg/m^3.

mcqs.q: A rectangular block measures 0.30 m by 0.20 m by 0.10 m. What is its volume?
options: 0.6 m³
6 m³
mcqs.explain: Volume of a cuboid = length x width x height = 0.30 x 0.20 x 0.10 = 0.006 m^3.

mcqs.q: A balance shows the mass of a block as 250 g. Which value should be used for m to obtain a density in kg/m³?
options: 250 000 kg, the reading multiplied by 1000
250 kg, the balance reading itself
2.5 N, the weight the balance is showing
0.25 kg, the reading divided by 1000
mcqs.explain: The equation needs mass in kilograms, and 250 g is 250 / 1000 = 0.25 kg.

mcqs.q: A solid aluminium bar is cut exactly in half. What is the density of each half?
options: Half the original value, since each piece has half the mass.
A quarter of the original value, since mass times volume is used.
A little lower, since each half now weighs less.
The same as the whole bar, because mass and volume both halve.
mcqs.explain: Density is a property of the material. Halving the mass and the volume together leaves the ratio unchanged.

mcqs.q: Which statement describes the arrangement of particles in a solid, a liquid and a gas?
options: Solid: regular and touching; liquid: evenly spaced out; gas: far apart.
Solid: small particles; liquid: larger ones; gas: the largest of all.
Solid: regular with wide gaps; liquid: random and touching; gas: random.
Solid: regular and touching; liquid: random but touching; gas: random and far apart.
mcqs.explain: This matches the particle model: solids and liquids both have particles in contact, and only the gas has widely separated particles.

mcqs.q: A student is drawing simple particle diagrams. Which drawing models a liquid correctly?
options: Circles of one size in a neat grid, evenly spaced.
Circles of one size touching, with no pattern.
Circles drawn larger than those in the solid diagram.
Circles spread far apart and scattered across the box.
mcqs.explain: In a liquid the particles are still in contact, as in a solid, but the arrangement is random so they can slide past one another.

mcqs.q: Why is the density of steam so much lower than the density of liquid water?
options: Its molecules are much further apart, so that mass fills more space.
Its molecules are lighter and smaller than those in the liquid water, too.
Some of the water's mass is destroyed when the liquid is boiled away.
Each molecule swells up as it is heated, so the steam weighs less.
mcqs.explain: The particle model explains density differences through spacing: the molecules are unchanged, but each cubic metre of steam holds far fewer of them.

mcqs.q: Ice floats on liquid water. What does this show about ice, and why?
options: It is less dense, because its molecules are held slightly further apart.
It is denser, because the solid state of a substance is always the denser one.
It is lighter, because a little mass is lost as the water freezes.
It has smaller molecules than water, which is what makes it rise.
mcqs.explain: Water is unusual: freezing locks the molecules into an open arrangement, so the same mass occupies a larger volume and the density falls to about 920 kg/m^3.

mcqs.q: A student is finding the density of a rectangular metal block. Which measurements are needed?
options: The mass from a balance, and the length of one side from a ruler.
The mass from a balance, and the length, width and height from a ruler.
The mass from a balance, and the area of one face from a ruler.
The weight in newtons, and the three dimensions from a ruler.
mcqs.explain: For a regularly shaped object the specification expects the volume to come from its dimensions, so all three lengths are needed along with the mass.

mcqs.q: A measuring cylinder holds 50 cm³ of water. A stone is lowered in and the level rises to 128 cm³. What is the volume of the stone?
options: 178 cm³, the two cylinder readings added
128 cm³, the final reading on the cylinder
78 cm³, the rise in the water level
50 cm³, the water already in the cylinder
mcqs.explain: The volume of an irregular object is the volume of water it displaces, which is the final reading minus the starting reading: 128 - 50 = 78 cm^3.

mcqs.q: A student measures the density of cooking oil with a measuring cylinder on a balance. Which mass is divided by the volume of oil?
options: The mass of the measuring cylinder once the oil has been poured in.
The mass of cylinder and oil minus the mass of the empty cylinder.
The mass of the empty measuring cylinder before the oil is added.
The mass of the empty cylinder added to the mass of cylinder and oil.
mcqs.explain: Only the oil occupies the measured volume, so the mass of the glass must be subtracted before dividing.

mcqs.q: Which instrument is most suitable for measuring the diameter of a copper wire about 0.4 mm across?
options: Vernier callipers, since they read in mm too.
A millimetre rule, estimated by eye.
A micrometer, reading to 0.01 mm.
Any of them, since all read in mm.
mcqs.explain: The resolution needs to be small compared with 0.4 mm. A micrometer reading to 0.01 mm measures the diameter to about two per cent.

mcqs.q: A sealed container holds 200 g of ice. The container is left until all the ice has melted. What does the balance read now?
options: 200 g, because melting rearranges the particles but removes none.
Less than 200 g, because some of the ice gets used up as it melts.
More than 200 g, since liquid water is denser than solid ice.
100 g, since the water takes up far less room than the ice.
mcqs.explain: Mass is conserved in a change of state. The container is sealed, so nothing can enter or leave.

mcqs.q: Solid carbon dioxide sublimates in an open dish on a balance and the reading falls to zero. Has any mass been destroyed?
options: Yes, subliming uses the solid up, so that mass has gone for good now.
No, but gases weigh nothing at all, so the reading had to fall away.
Yes, because a gas is a new substance made out of that solid.
No, the gas has spread into the room and is not on the balance.
mcqs.explain: Sublimation is a change of state, so mass is conserved. The balance reads zero only because the carbon dioxide is no longer on the pan.

mcqs.q: Why is boiling water classed as a physical change rather than a chemical change?
options: Steam is a new substance, but a very easy one to turn back.
Physical changes are reversible and chemical changes are not.
Boiling can be undone, so it cannot be a chemical change.
The steam is still water; cooling gives the liquid back.
mcqs.explain: In a physical change no new substance is formed, and reversing the change recovers the original properties.
